MARKET RESEARCH
Commercial
Research and analysis · September 2026
COMMERCIAL MARKET
What this deck covers
—  The $10 million+ Performance Property model portfolio is dominated by commercial property. The purpose of commercial property within the investment portfolio is to produce low-risk income, alongside residential property which focuses on capital growth.
—  When investing into any asset, it is critical to understand the return expected for each unit of risk taken on. Commercial property is highly desirable based on this criteria.
—  With a positive inflation target, a growing population, strong household expenditure, and building prices increasing, commercial real estate must rise long-term
In this deck — risk premium · container trade · retail spending · population · healthcare · yields

COMMERCIAL MARKET
Online share of retail — Australia v United States
Australia: ABS online retail turnover as a share of total retail turnover. United States: US Census Bureau e-commerce sales as a share of total retail sales, annual average of the four quarterly readings — which reproduces the Census published annual figure (16.1% for 2024).
Not like-for-like: the ABS base excludes motor vehicles and fuel but includes cafés and takeaway; the US base includes motor vehicles and fuel but excludes food services. Both differences flatter Australia, so the real gap is wider than shown.

performanceproperty.com.au
Midpoint yield, Q2 2026. CBD super prime and regional centre removed at request — worth noting those were the series carrying the dispersion (CBD super prime spans 175bp across the states, regional centres 127bp). Prime large format spans 30bp, four of five states inside 10bp.

COMMERCIAL MARKET
Industrial rents by grade — prime v secondary (JLL)
Solid is prime, dashed is secondary; colour is the city. Since Q1 2015 secondary has outgrown prime in four of the five capitals — Melbourne +112% v +86%, Adelaide +80% v +59%, Brisbane +64% v +59%, Perth +30% v +21% — so the quality premium has compressed everywhere except Sydney, where the two ran together (+107% v +103%).
Face rents, not effective. Incentives rose over the same period (Brisbane 8.3% to 19.6%, Sydney 12.8% to 20.8%), so income growth is lower than these lines — Perth is +21% on face and +7% effective. Adelaide secondary has gaps where every precinct failed the plausibility filter. Source: JLL.
performanceproperty.com.au
COMMERCIAL MARKET
Secondary v prime rent — distance from long-run average
performanceproperty.com.au
Zero is each city’s own long-run normal, so the lines are comparable even though the averages are not — Sydney secondary runs 92.7% of prime over the period, Melbourne 72.3%. Above zero means older stock is dearer relative to prime than it usually is, so the discount for buying secondary has narrowed. Read with slide 36. When replacement cost rises above what prime trades for, building new stops paying and secondary has to catch up — that is the mechanism behind this line.
COMMERCIAL MARKET
Land against rents — land $/sqm per $1 of prime net rent (JLL)
performanceproperty.com.au
Land is $/sqm of land on a 2,000sqm lot; rent is $/sqm of building — so read this as relative movement, not a literal years-of-rent figure. Melbourne’s step down in late 2002 is a change in what JLL measured, not a fall in land value.
COMMERCIAL MARKET
Sydney prime industrial — pricing re-rated first, rents followed
Both indexed to Q1 2015 = 100. Capital value = rent × (1 ÷ yield), so the two lines are the only two things that move it. To Q2 2022 the repricing was almost entirely the yield: the multiple reached 203 while rent had moved to 136. Since then the multiple has fallen to 139 while rent has run to 207.
Same shape in every market at its own peak (multiple, rent index): Melbourne 204 / 116 · Perth 165 / 85 · Brisbane 162 / 105 · Adelaide 152 / 117. Perth’s rents FELL while values rose. Source: JLL; yields are the precinct-average midpoint.

What the GFC took — peak-to-trough fall by measure
performanceproperty.com.au
Peak is each city’s own, searched across 2006–2008, with the trough after it to end-2012. Income barely moved while the assets did — and secondary values fell harder than prime in four of five cities.
COMMERCIAL MARKET
How long the recovery took — capital values, Q4 2007 = 100
performanceproperty.com.au
Rebased to Q4 2007 = 100, which is also the peak for four of the five cities; Melbourne peaked a quarter later, 1% higher. Sydney and Melbourne take until Q1 2015 to regain the peak, Brisbane Q2 2015 — seven years of grinding sideways. Perth is still 15% below its 2007 level at the end of 2018.
